title: Explicit inverse image of a coefficient tower
statement:
variable {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
  [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C]
  (B : ℕ → Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r})
  (τ : ∀ n : ℕ, B (n + 1) ⟶ B n)

theorem geometricCoefficientTower
    {C' : Type c} [Category.{v} C'] [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C']
    (J' : GrothendieckTopology C')
    (uInv : Sheaf J (Type (max c v r)) ⥤ Sheaf J' (Type (max c v r)))
    [PreservesFiniteLimits uInv] :
    ∃ (F : ℕ → Sheaf J' CommRingCat.{max c v r})
      (σ : ∀ n : ℕ, F (n + 1) ⟶ F n)
      (I : ∀ n : ℕ, SheafOfModules.AlgebraicInverseImage uInv (B n) (F n)),
      ∀ n : ℕ,
        uInv.map ((sheafCompose J (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{max c v r})).map
            (τ n)) ≫ (I n).ringUnderlying.hom =
          (I (n + 1)).ringUnderlying.hom ≫
            (sheafCompose J' (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{max c v r})).map (σ n)

proof.text: Transport each commutative ring object and its module objects along the finite-product-preserving functor. The existing concrete ringImage and algebraicImage definitions give the coefficient rings and algebraic inverse images. Their underlying identifications and graph laws are part of those constructions.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module; transport of ring and module operation graphs, applied to the coefficient system of Zheng Construction 4.1.

proof.text: For each adjacent transition apply the original ring homomorphism to an addition, multiplication or unit graph, then apply the target algebraic inverse-image graph law. The structuralMap helper bundles the resulting underlying map as a ring-sheaf morphism with specified underlying map. Cancel the underlying isomorphism to obtain compatibility. The Lean proof uses the already proved graph-bundling helper and concrete definitions of CochainCompositeAlgebraic, rather than assuming its composite-existence theorem.
